subject: using lubridate to determine whether any of a set of time intervals overlap

messages.author: 2b27719db7267c87
messages.subject: using lubridate to determine whether any of a set of time intervals overlap
parts:
Hi all,

I am using the lubridate package to work with a set of time intervals, like this:

require(lubridate)
int1 <- new_interval(ymd_hms("2014-07-12 05:48:02"), ymd_hms("2014-07-13 05:48:02"))
int2 <- new_interval(ymd_hms("2014-07-12 10:48:02"), ymd_hms("2014-07-13 07:48:02"))
int3 <- new_interval(ymd_hms("2014-07-11 10:48:02"), ymd_hms("2014-07-12 01:48:02"))
int4 <- new_interval(NA, NA)
ints <- c(int1, int2, int3, int4)

I would like to determine whether any combination of two intervals in this set overlap with each other.  The int_overlaps() function can check each interval against the rest of the list, but it can't seem to check all combinations.

int_overlaps(int1, ints)

Since the real vector of time intervals I am working with is much longer than this one, I would like to automate the process of checking all combinations for overlaps.  So, I created a for-loop that does it.

results <- matrix(rep(NA, 16), ncol=4)
for (i in 1:length(ints)) {
  results[i, ] <- int_overlaps(ints[i], ints)}

But, does anyone know of a vectorized way to do this?  I have tried using combn() and lapply() without success.  They seem to unclass the intervals, so they are no longer intervals.

Thanks!

Bonnie
